title: Scenario
description: Definition of a reusable step sequence that can be called by name from any testcase in any suite, avoiding duplication of common flows. A scenario's steps do not carry their own 'dataset' — the scenario is called with a single dataset (the caller's 'dataset', shallow-merged over this scenario's 'default_dataset', caller's fields winning on collision), and every step's template renders directly against that one resolved dataset.

name.description: Unique name used to reference this scenario.

description.description: Optional free-text description of what the scenario does.

default_dataset.description: Default values used to render this scenario's steps, shallow-merged with the caller's 'dataset' at call time (caller's fields win on collision). If the caller omits 'dataset' entirely, default_dataset is used as-is. Either a literal inline object, or a string naming a separately-defined dataset (see dataset.schema.json). If neither the caller's dataset nor default_dataset is present, calling this scenario is an error.

steps.description: Ordered list of steps to execute for this scenario. Each entry is either a template-step (client + template, rendered against the scenario's resolved dataset — see the top-level description) or a call into another reusable scenario (scenario + optional dataset), allowing scenarios to be composed.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for the step, shown in results. Defaults to "<client>: <template>" if omitted.

client.description: Name of the registered client that sends the rendered template. Must match a client registered in the Maestro client registry at runtime, and must be listed in the template's own 'clients'.

template.description: Name of a reusable template whose placeholders are filled in directly from the scenario's resolved dataset and sent via 'client'. This step does not declare its own dataset.

assert.description: Optional checks run against this step's result after it executes. Each check is dispatched to a registered assertion provider.

save.description: Optional values to extract from this step's response into named state, for later steps to reference via interpolation.

name.description: Optional human-readable label for this scenario call, shown in results. Defaults to the scenario name if omitted.

scenario.description: Name of another reusable scenario to run inline at this point.

dataset.description: Input values passed to the nested scenario's parameters. Either a literal inline object, or a string naming a separately-defined dataset. Merges with the nested scenario's own default_dataset the same way a top-level call does.

assert.description: Optional checks run against this nested scenario call's result after it executes. Each check is dispatched to a registered assertion provider.

provider.description: Name of the registered assertion provider that interprets 'properties' and performs the check (e.g. "db" to look up a row and validate it, "http_response" to check the last response's shape). Must match a provider registered in the Maestro assertion-provider registry at runtime.

properties.description: Configuration passed to the assertion provider. Shape is defined entirely by the provider itself, not by this schema — e.g. a 'db' provider might expect {table, where, exists}, an 'http_response' provider might expect {path, equals}. May reference the scenario's resolved dataset via interpolation (e.g. "{{order_id}}").

path.description: Path into this step's response identifying the value to extract (e.g. "$.token").

as.description: Name to store the extracted value under, referenceable in later steps via interpolation (e.g. "{{auth_token}}").

examples.name: login_and_get_token
examples.description: Logs in as the given user and saves the returned auth token to test state as 'auth_token'.
